title: Gen 7 candidate · phase 1: cross-matched feedback, 2,000 boards a pair
pending: Acceptance of Gen 7 by Max. Not given yet. It turns mostly on policy v4 and on the tree's budgets (`max_solves`, `path_solves`, and the compute the standard bot may spend at tricks 3 to 6).

Final tree parameters of 7s-32: `root_margin`, `trust`, `path`, `tricks`, `breadth`, `mass`. The values below are the candidate of 11 November 23:30 UTC, from one bench set and a short smoke match (docs/gen7_candidate_2026-11-11.md).

Audits in the anchor pairs (7s-32 against ben64, ben, 5RZ32 and 1): Max wants them off. BEN boards already carry none (`ben_audit`). There is no per-pair switch for 5RZ32 and 1 in this runtime; it has to be added before those two pairs run, or they run with the cohort's audits.

Stop rule: this phase ends when every pair has 2,000 completed boards (10,000 in all). The plan format has no per-pair target; the producer has to watch `by_pair` and cut over to phase 2 with a new cohort.
notes: Candidate, not a launch. `launch_enabled` is false and `pending` is not empty, so ops/prepare_gen7_alpha.py refuses this file. The go-ahead will be a later commit that settles `pending`.

A Gen 7 bot is its Gen 6 base bot (same bidder, lead net, scorer, layouts and sample count) with the gen7 engine and policy v4. docs/gen7_alpha_2026-11-11.md explains every setting; docs/gen7_candidate_2026-11-11.md is the notice this file belongs to.
Audit and capture settings (tie audits, gap forks, room seeds) are carried over from the source run, not set here.
Phase 1 comes first so that there is feedback against known opponents before volume. Every board here is two tables on one deal.
